items.q: Which command installs Playwright?
items.e: npm init playwright@latest — initializes the project, installs @playwright/test and browsers via the setup wizard.

items.q: Which command runs all Playwright tests?
items.e: npx playwright test — runs all tests in the project. Options: --headed, --debug, --ui, --project=chromium.

items.q: Which command opens Playwright UI Mode?
items.e: npx playwright test --ui — opens the interactive UI for running, debugging and viewing test traces.

items.q: Which command installs the Playwright browsers?
items.e: npx playwright install — downloads Chromium, Firefox, WebKit. npx playwright install chromium — a single browser.

items.q: Which file is the entry point of Playwright configuration?
items.e: playwright.config.ts (or .js) — the main config: timeout, baseURL, projects, reporter, use etc.

items.q: What does a basic Playwright test look like?
items.e: test("name", async ({ page }) => {}) — the basic unit. page is a built-in fixture. async/await is mandatory.

items.q: What are test fixtures in Playwright?
o: Objects automatically provided to tests via parameter destructuring
items.e: Fixtures ({ page, context, browser, request }) — created and destroyed automatically. Custom ones via test.extend().

items.q: What is the difference between test.describe and test?
o: describe — groups tests; test — an individual test case
test is a group, describe is a single test
items.e: test.describe("Group", () => { test("case1", ...) }) — a logical group. Can be nested. Affects report names.

items.q: What are test.beforeEach and test.afterEach?
o: Hooks that run before/after every test in a describe block
items.e: beforeEach/afterEach run before/after every test in the current describe. beforeAll/afterAll — once per group.

items.q: How do you run only one test in Playwright?
items.e: test.only("name", ...) — runs only this test. describe.only() — only this group. Alternative: npx playwright test -g "name".

items.q: How do you navigate to a URL in Playwright?
items.e: await page.goto(url) — navigation. Returns a Response. goto("/path") + baseURL from the config = the full URL.

items.q: How do you click an element in Playwright?
items.e: page.click(selector) and page.locator(selector).click() — both are valid. The locator style is the recommended modern approach.

items.q: How do you type text into a field in Playwright?
items.e: fill() — clears and inputs the text at once (recommended). type() — simulates key-by-key typing (for special effects).

items.q: What is the difference between page.fill() and page.type()?
o: fill() inserts the text at once; type() simulates typing character by character with delays
items.e: fill() — fast direct input. type() — simulates real typing with keyboard events. fill() is better for most tests.

items.q: How do you press a keyboard key?
items.e: page.keyboard.press("Enter") — global. page.press(selector, "Enter") — focuses the element and presses the key.

items.q: How do you hover over an element?
items.e: page.hover() and locator.hover() — both move the mouse over the element. Useful for dropdown menus.

items.q: How do you select an option in a <select>?
items.e: selectOption(selector, {value: "v"}) or {label: "l"} or {index: 0} — flexible option selection in a select.

items.q: How do you upload a file via an input?
items.e: setInputFiles(selector, path) and locator.setInputFiles(path) — upload a file via input[type=file].

items.q: How do you drag and drop an element?
items.e: page.dragAndDrop(source, target) and locator.dragTo(targetLocator) — both ways to drag and drop.

items.q: How do you scroll to an element?
items.e: locator.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded() — scrolls only if the element is outside the viewport. Better than page.evaluate scrollIntoView.

items.q: Which Playwright locator is recommended for finding by role?
items.e: getByRole() — the priority locator. Resilient to markup changes, matches the accessibility tree.

items.q: How do you find an element by text?
items.e: getByText("Welcome") and locator("text=Welcome") — both find the element by its visible text.

items.q: How do you find an element by placeholder?
items.e: getByPlaceholder("Email") — a semantic locator for fields with a placeholder attribute.

items.q: How do you find an element by label?
items.e: getByLabel("Password") — finds the input associated with a label. The right approach for forms.

items.q: How do you find an element by test-id attribute?
items.e: getByTestId() looks for data-testid by default. Configurable: testIdAttribute: "data-cy".

items.q: How do you find an element inside another element?
items.e: Chaining: locator(".parent").locator(".child") and the CSS selector ".parent .child" — both find the nested element.

items.q: What is locator.filter()?
o: Filters a locator collection by a condition (text, nested element)
items.e: locator.filter({ hasText: "Admin" }) or filter({ has: page.getByRole("checkbox") }) — narrows the locator among matches.

items.q: How do you get the first/last element of a collection?
items.e: locator.first(), locator.last(), locator.nth(n) — element selection from a collection. nth(-1) — the last element.

items.q: How do you wait for an element to appear?
items.e: locator.waitFor({ state: "visible" }) — waits for the element. Default state is "visible". Also: attached, hidden, detached.

items.q: How do you get the number of elements in a collection?
items.e: await locator.count() — returns Promise<number>. For an assertion: await expect(locator).toHaveCount(3).

items.q: Which assertion library is built into Playwright?
o: expect() from @playwright/test — web-first assertions with auto-waiting
items.e: expect() — built-in web-first assertions that automatically wait for the condition until timeout. No separate waitFor needed.

items.q: How do you assert that an element is visible?
items.e: expect(locator).toBeVisible() — waits and checks visibility. Auto-retries until actionTimeout.

items.q: How do you assert an element's text?
items.e: toHaveText() — exact match (or regex). toContainText() — checks substring containment. Both auto-wait.

items.q: How do you assert an attribute value?
items.e: expect(locator).toHaveAttribute(name, value) — attribute assertion with auto-waiting.

items.q: How do you assert the page URL?
items.e: expect(page).toHaveURL(url|regex) — a web-first URL assertion that waits for navigation.

items.q: How do you assert the page title?
items.e: expect(page).toHaveTitle(title|regex) — checks the page <title> with auto-waiting.

items.q: How do you assert that a checkbox is checked?
items.e: expect(locator).toBeChecked() — checks the checked state of a checkbox/radio. toBeChecked({ checked: false }) — the opposite.

items.q: How do you assert that an element is disabled?
items.e: expect(locator).toBeDisabled() — checks the disabled attribute. toBeEnabled() — the opposite.

items.q: How do you assert an input field's value?
items.e: expect(locator).toHaveValue(value|regex) — checks the value of an input/select/textarea.

items.q: How do you get an input field's value?
items.e: await locator.inputValue() — returns the current value of an input/textarea/select. getAttribute("value") may return the initial value.

items.q: How do you intercept and modify a network request?
items.e: page.route("**/api/users", route => route.fulfill({ body: json })) — intercepts the request and returns a mock response.

items.q: How do you block a network request?
items.e: route.abort() — cancels the request. Useful for blocking ads, analytics, or testing offline behavior.

items.q: How do you wait for a network request?
items.e: waitForRequest() and waitForResponse() — wait for a specific request/response. Usually: const [response] = await Promise.all([page.waitForResponse(...), action]).

items.q: How do you capture all network requests during a test?
items.e: page.on("request", handler) and page.on("response", handler) — network event listeners for traffic monitoring.

items.q: What is APIRequestContext in Playwright?
o: An HTTP client for API tests without a browser
items.e: The request fixture (APIRequestContext) — makes HTTP requests without a UI: await request.get(url), post(), put(). Integrated with Playwright.

items.q: How do you make an API request in a Playwright test?
items.e: request.get/post/put/delete() — via the request fixture, or page.request for requests within the browser session (with cookies).

items.q: How do you configure baseURL in Playwright?
items.e: playwright.config.ts: use: { baseURL: "https://example.com" } — allows goto("/path") instead of the full URL.

items.q: How do you configure multiple browsers (projects)?
items.e: projects in playwright.config.ts: each project is a separate browser/device. Tests run in each of them.

items.q: How do you configure headless mode?
o: use: { headless: true } in the config, or --headed in the CLI
items.e: playwright.config.ts: use: { headless: false } to show the browser. CLI: npx playwright test --headed. Default is headless: true.

items.q: How do you set a global test timeout?
items.e: timeout in playwright.config.ts — per-test timeout (ms). expect.timeout — for assertions. navigationTimeout — for navigation.

items.q: What is globalSetup in Playwright?
o: A file executed once before all tests (login, seed DB)
items.e: globalSetup: "./global-setup.ts" in the config — runs once. Useful for auth: save the state to a file.

items.q: What is storageState in Playwright?
o: Saved browser state (cookies, localStorage) for reuse
items.e: storageState saves cookies and localStorage after login. Passed to the context: { storageState: "auth.json" } — no login in every test.

items.q: How do you configure video recording of tests?
items.e: use: { video: "on" | "off" | "retain-on-failure" | "on-first-retry" } in the config or a project.

items.q: How do you configure screenshots?
items.e: use: { screenshot: "on" | "off" | "only-on-failure" } — automatic screenshots. Also: await page.screenshot({ path: "shot.png" }).

items.q: What is a Playwright Trace?
o: A detailed recording of the test run: actions, screenshots, network, console
items.e: A trace is a ZIP with every test step, screenshots and network. Open it: npx playwright show-trace trace.zip or trace.playwright.dev.

items.q: How do you enable trace recording?
items.e: use: { trace: "on" | "off" | "on-first-retry" | "retain-on-failure" } — on-first-retry is recommended for CI.

items.q: How do you open the Playwright Trace Viewer?
items.e: npx playwright show-trace trace.zip or online at trace.playwright.dev — a detailed interactive view of every step.

items.q: How do you run a test in debug mode?
o: PWDEBUG=1 npx playwright test or npx playwright test --debug
items.e: --debug or PWDEBUG=1 opens the Playwright Inspector — step-by-step execution with locator highlighting and logs.

items.q: What does await page.pause() do?
o: Pauses execution and opens the Playwright Inspector for debugging
Sets a breakpoint in the browser
items.e: page.pause() — a breakpoint in the test. Opens the Inspector where you can examine the page state and resume.

items.q: How do you record a test with Playwright Codegen?
items.e: npx playwright codegen https://example.com — opens a browser and generates test code from your actions in real time.

items.q: What is a BrowserContext in Playwright?
o: An isolated browser session with its own cookies/localStorage — like a profile
items.e: BrowserContext — an isolated session. Every test gets a clean context. One context can hold several pages (tabs).

items.q: How do you open a new tab?
items.e: context.newPage() — opens a new tab in the same context (shared cookies). browser.newPage() — a new context.

items.q: How do you handle a popup window?
items.e: Promise.all([waitForEvent("popup"), triggerAction()]) — waits for the popup simultaneously with the action that opens it.

items.q: How do you handle a dialog (alert/confirm)?
items.e: page.on("dialog", dialog => dialog.accept()) — subscribe to the dialog event. Must be registered BEFORE the action that opens it.

items.q: How do you switch between tabs?
o: Get the page via context.pages() and work with it
items.e: context.pages() returns all open pages. Just use the page object you need — there is no "switchTo" method.

items.q: How do you implement a Page Object in Playwright?
o: A class with readonly page: Page in the constructor and action methods
items.e: class LoginPage { constructor(private page: Page) {} async login(u,p) { await this.page.fill(...) } } — the standard POM.

items.q: How do you wire a Page Object through a fixture?
o: test.extend<{ loginPage: LoginPage }>({ loginPage: async ({ page }, use) => { await use(new LoginPage(page)) } })
test.use({ loginPage: new LoginPage(page) }) in the config so Playwright creates the page object
import LoginPage in every test and call loginPage.use(page) before the describe block
page.extend(LoginPage).fixture("loginPage") and pass the class directly to test.describe()
items.e: test.extend() lets you provide a Page Object as a fixture — injected into the test automatically without a manual new.

items.q: How do you type locators in a TypeScript Page Object?
items.e: private readonly submitBtn: Locator = this.page.getByRole("button", { name: "Submit" }) — a typed Locator class field.

items.q: What is async/await in the context of Playwright?
o: Promise syntax — await waits for completion before the next step
items.e: Almost all Playwright methods return Promises. await guarantees sequential execution. Without await the action won't finish before the next line.

items.q: What is an interface in TypeScript?
o: A description of an object's structure without implementation — for type checking
items.e: interface User { name: string; age: number } — describes an object's shape. No runtime existence, compile-time checking only.

items.q: What is type vs interface in TypeScript?
o: type — broader (union, intersection, primitives); interface — objects only, supports declaration merging
interface supports unions and primitive aliases; type only works with class-like objects without merging
type and interface are fully identical, but interface compiles faster in the JavaScript runtime
type is only needed for enum values; interface is used only for React components
items.e: type can do: union (A|B), intersection (A&B), mapped types. interface: declaration merging (augmentation), better for OOP.

items.q: What is an enum in TypeScript?
items.e: enum Direction { Up, Down } — compiles to a JS object. const enum — inlined (no JS code). Useful for states, roles, statuses.

items.q: What are generics in TypeScript?
o: Parameterized types for type-safe functions and classes
items.e: function wrap<T>(val: T): T[] { return [val] } — T is inferred from the argument. Safer than any, more flexible than a concrete type.

items.q: What are union types in TypeScript?
o: A type that can be one of several: string | number
items.e: string | number | null — the variable can be any of the types. Narrowing (if typeof x === "string") refines the type in the block.

items.q: What is optional chaining (?.) in TypeScript/JS?
o: user?.address?.city — returns undefined instead of an error when an intermediate value is null/undefined
user ? address : city — a shorthand ternary operator for choosing between two values
user.address.city! — a forced type assertion guaranteeing the field is not null
user && address && city — syntax that automatically creates nested objects when missing
items.e: obj?.prop?.method?.() — safe navigation through a potentially null/undefined chain. Replaces if (obj && obj.prop && ...).

items.q: What is nullish coalescing (??) in TypeScript/JS?
o: value ?? defaultValue — returns the default only when value is null or undefined
items.e: null ?? "default" → "default". 0 ?? "default" → 0. Differs from ||: 0 || "default" → "default" (because 0 is falsy).

items.q: What are decorators in TypeScript?
o: Annotations (@) that modify the behavior of classes, methods, fields
items.e: @Component, @Injectable, @Test — decorators modify a class/method at compile time. Require experimentalDecorators in tsconfig.

items.q: How do you run a test on a mobile device?
items.e: projects: [{ name: "mobile", use: { ...devices["iPhone 13"] } }] — emulates a mobile viewport, UA and touch.

items.q: What is devices in Playwright?
o: A set of presets for emulating mobile devices (viewport, userAgent, touch)
items.e: import { devices } from "@playwright/test" — devices["Pixel 5"], devices["iPhone 13 Pro"] etc. Include viewport, UA, hasTouch.

items.q: How do you emulate geolocation?
items.e: context or use: { geolocation: { latitude, longitude }, permissions: ["geolocation"] } — GPS position emulation.

items.q: How do you emulate dark mode?
items.e: use: { colorScheme: "dark" | "light" | "no-preference" } — emulates the prefers-color-scheme media query.

items.q: How do you take a full-page screenshot?
items.e: page.screenshot({ fullPage: true }) — a screenshot of the whole page including scroll. path — where to save it.

items.q: How do you screenshot a specific element?
items.e: locator.screenshot() — a screenshot of just the element. Useful for visual comparison of a specific component.

items.q: What is visual comparison in Playwright?
o: expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() — compares against a baseline screenshot
items.e: expect(page).toHaveScreenshot("name.png") — pixel-perfect comparison. The first run creates the snapshot. A diff → the test fails.

items.q: How do you run tests in parallel in Playwright?
o: workers: 4 or fullyParallel: true in the config
items.e: workers: N (the number of parallel workers) and fullyParallel: true (parallelism within a file) in playwright.config.ts.

items.q: What is test.describe.parallel?
o: Runs the tests inside the describe in parallel
A fullyParallel analog for a block
items.e: test.describe.parallel("group", () => { test(...); test(...) }) — all tests in the group run in parallel.

items.q: What is test.describe.serial?
o: Runs the group's tests sequentially, stopping at the first failure
items.e: test.describe.serial() — tests run sequentially. If one fails — the rest are skipped.

items.q: How do you run tests for a specific browser only?
items.e: npx playwright test --project=chromium — runs only the project named "chromium". Multiple allowed: --project=chromium --project=firefox.

items.q: How do you configure retries for failing tests?
items.e: retries: 2 in the config — reruns a failed test up to 2 more times. npx playwright test --retries=2 — the CLI variant.

items.q: What is the default reporter in Playwright?
items.e: Default: list in the terminal. reporter: [["html"]] in the config generates an HTML report. npx playwright show-report opens it.

items.q: How do you attach Allure to Playwright?
items.e: npm install allure-playwright, then in the config: reporter: [["allure-playwright", { outputFolder: "allure-results" }]].

items.q: How do you run Playwright tests in Docker?
o: Use the official mcr.microsoft.com/playwright image with pre-installed browsers
items.e: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.x.x — the official Docker image with all browsers and dependencies for CI.

items.q: What is expect.soft() in Playwright?
o: A soft assertion — the test continues after a failure, all failures are reported at the end
An assertion with a smaller timeout
items.e: expect.soft(locator).toBeVisible() — doesn't stop the test on failure. All soft assertion failures are collected and shown together.
